Disclosure  to  Promote  the  Right  To  Information 

Whereas  the  Parliament  of  India  has  set  out  to  provide  a  practical  regime  of  right  to 
information  for  citizens  to  secure  access  to  information  under  the  control  of  public  authorities, 
in  order  to  promote  transparency  and  accountability  in  the  working  of  every  public  authority, 
and  whereas  the  attached  publication  of  the  Bureau  of  Indian  Standards  is  of  particular  interest 
to  the  public,  particularly  disadvantaged  communities  and  those  engaged  in  the  pursuit  of 
education  and  knowledge,  the  attached  public  safety  standard  is  made  available  to  promote  the 
timely  dissemination  of  this  information  in  an  accurate  manner  to  the  public.

Indian  Standard 

SPECIFICATION  FOR 
PORTABLE  PNEUMATIC  RIVET  CUTTERS 

,  r-    i  n     .  .       x  ( Reaffirmed  2005 ) 

(  First  Revision  ) 


1.  Scope  — Covers  the  requirements  for  portable  pneumatic  rivet  cutters  suitable  for  cutting  steel 
rivets  up  to  27  mm  in  diameter  according  to  IS  :  2155-1982  'Cold  forged  solid  steel  rivets  for  hot  closing 
(6  to  16  mm  diameter  )  ( first  revision  )'  and  IS  :  1929-1982  'Hot  forged  steel  rivets  for  hot  closing 
( 12  to  36  mm  diameter )  ( first  revision  )'. 

2.  Terminology 

2.1  Rivet  Cutter —  A  percussive  piston  tool  in  which  potential  energy  of  compressed  air  acting  on  a 
free  piston  is  converted  into  kinetic  energy.  The  piston,  having  this  converted  kinetic  energy,  strikes  on 
the  rivet  cutting  chisel  thus  imparting  this  energy  to  the  cutting  chisel  for  the  purpose  of  rivet  cutting. 

2.2  Retainer  —  A  device  which  holds  the  rivet  cutting  chisel  in  position  with  the  cutter  body. 

2.3  Gauge  Pressure  —  Steady  pressure  of  compressed  air  measured  within  three  metres  from  inlet  of 
rivet  cutter. 

2.4  Air  Consumption  —  Volume  of  air,  corrected  to  standard  atmospheric  conditions  of  testing 
according  to  IS:  196-1966  'Atmospheric  conditions  for  testing  (  revised)'  consumed  by  rivet  cutter 
during  pellet  test  without  fluctuation  of  pressure  during  the  test. 

3.  Sizes  and  Main  Dimensions

Note  —  If  the  rivets  are  made  of  other  materials  manufacturer  may  be  consulted  for  rivet  cutting  capacity. 
4,  General  Requirements 

4.1  A  suitable  retainer,  preferably  of  retaining  spring  type,  shall  be  provided  to  hold  the  cutting  chisel 
in  position. 

4.2  Handles 

4.2.1  Type  A  —  Open  handle  with  thumb  lever  throttle  control  (  see  Fig.  1  ) 

4.2.2  Type  B  — Closed  handle  with  thumb  lever  throttle  control  (see  Fig.  2  ). 

4.2.3  Type  C  —  Closed  handle  with  finger  lever  throttle  control  (see  Fig.  3  ). 

4.3  Air  Inlet  Connection 

4.3.1  Air  inlet  connection  shall  be  fitted  with  an  air  strainer  or  screen  forming  a  part  of  the 
nipple/bush  which  shall  be  effective  in  retaining  solid  particles  in  compressed  air  supply  and  shall  be 
easily  cleanable. 

4.3.2  Air  inlet  connection  size  for  all  sizes  of  pneumatic  rivet  cutter  shall  be  Re  \  conforming  to 
IS:  554-1975  'Dimensions  for  pipe  threads  where  pressure  tight  joints  are  required  on  the  threads 
( second  revision )'.

4.4  The  rivet  cutters  shall  be  of  such  a  design  that  the  exhaust  of  compressed  air  from  the  tool  may  be 
directed  in  any  direction  depending  upon  the  requirements. 

4.5  An  instruction  manual  shall  be  supplied  with  each  tool.  Data  to  provided  in  the  manual  shall  be  in 
accordance  with  Indian  Standard  Technical  supply  conditions  for  pneumatic  tools'  ( under 
preparation  ). 

5.  Designation  — A  pneumatic  rivet  cutter  of  nominal  size  '20'  and  having  'Type  B'  handle  shall  be 
designated  as: 


Rivet  Cutter  20B  IS  :  7978 


6.  Tests 


6.1  Pellet  Test  —  The  rivet  cutter  shall  be  operated  on  a  test  rig  for  a  specified  period  to  beat  down  a 
cylindrical  pellet  of  steel.  The  compression  of  the  pellet  shall  be  measured  and  shall  be  within  the 
values  specified  in  6.1.4. 


6.1.1  The  test  rig  shall  consist  of  a  firm  and  solid  steel 
which  a  substantial  pot  shall  be  mounted  (  see  Fig.  4). 


base   having   a  hardened   steel   bush,    upon 


6.1.2  The  pellet  145  mm  in  diameter,  150  mm  in  length  and  made  of  steel  designation  20C8  of 
IS  :  1570  (Part  2  )-1979  'Schedules  for  wrought  steel:  Part  2  Carbon  steel  (unalloyed  steel)'  shall  be 
placed  vertically  in  the  pot    The  pellet  shall  have  hardness  of  125-150  HV. 

6.1.3  For  conducting  the  test,  the  rivet  cutter  fitted  with  a  blunt  steel  plunger  of  sufficient  hardness 
shall  be  placed  in  position  so  that  the  plunger  rests  on  the  pellet.  The  tool  shall  then  be  operated  for 
five  seconds  (  measured  with  a  stopwatch).  The  cutter  and  the  plunger  shall  then  be  removed  and 
pellet  withdrawn  from  the  pot. 

6.1.4  The  compression  of  the  pellet  shall  be  measured  with  micrometer  and  shall  be  within— 5  percent 
of  the  values  declared  by  the  manufacturers. 

6.2  Air  Consumption  Test  —  The  water  displacement  meter  or  any  other  equally  suitable  instrument 
shall  be  used  to  determine  the  quantity  of  air  consumed  per  minute  at  6'0  ±  0'5  bar  pressure  measured 
at  a  distance  of  not  more  than  three  metres  from  the  inlet  of  the  tool  while  the  pellet  test  is  being 
conducted  as  described  in  6.1.  The  air  consumption  corrected  to  atmospheric  conditions  of  testing 
according  to  IS  :  196-1966  shall  be  within  +5  percent  of  the  values  declared  by  the  manufacturer.

6.3  Endurance  Test 

6.3.1  For  type  approval  —  Each  sample  conforming  to  pellet  test  shall  be  run  in  the  test  rig  to 
disseminate  energy  for  100  h  in  the  manufacturers  test  room  ( 100  h  run  need  not  be  at  a  stretch  and 
may  be  done  over  a  period),  after  which  the  tool  shall  be  dismantled  and  all  parts  shall  be  examined. 
No  parts  shall  either  break  during  testing  or  be  found  broken,  cracked  or  deformed  on  examination. 

6.3.2  For  routine  testing  —  One  percent  the  minimum  being  one,  of  the  tools  on  order,  if  the  order 
is  for  50  pieces  or  more,  shall  be  run  on  the  test  rig  to  disseminate  ensrgy  in  the  manufacturer's  test 
room  for  15  h  (  15  h  run  need  not  be  at  a  stretch  and  may  be  done  over  a  period),  after  which 
the  tools  shall  be  dismantled  and  all  parts  shall  be  examined.  No  part  shall  either  break  during  testing 
or  be  found  broken,  cracked  or  deformed  on  examination. 

6.4  Each  rivet  cutter  shall  be  tested  for  easy  starting  and  stopping.  It  shall  also  be  tested  for  easy 
fitment  and  removal  of  the  rivet  cutting  chisel  in  the  bushing.  The  rivet  cutter  shall  show  no  flaws 
which  may  have  been  developed  during  testing. 

7.  Marking  —  Each  rivet  cutter  shall  be  marked  with  the  manufacturer's  name  or  trade-mark,  nominal 
size  and  year  of  manufacture. 

7.1  ISI  Certification  Marking  —  Details  available  with  the  Indian  Standards  Institution. 

8.  Packing  and  Packaging — Before  packing,  the  inlet  exhaust  and  other  openings  of  each  tool 
shall  be  adequately  protected/covered  against  ingress  of  dust  and  other  harmful  materials.  Packing  of 
rivet  cutters  shall  be  done  in  accordance  with  'Indian  Standard  Technical  supply  conditions  for 
pneumatic  tools'  (  under  preparation  ). 


EXPLANATORY     NOTE 

This  specification  was  first  issued  in  1976.  In  view  of  the  experience  gained  in  this  field,  the 
revision  has  been  taken  up.  Alterations  have  been  made  in  overall  length,  mass  and  pellet  size. 
Compression  of  pellet  and  air  consumption  requirements  have  been  toleranced  on  the  declared  values  of 
the  manufacturers.  This  standard  has  been  prepared  based  on  the  details  provided  by  the 
manufacturers  of  the  product. 


Printed  at  Arcee  Press,  New  Delhi,  India
